plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential damages exclusion, and Excluded Claims covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, and IP infringement. Check that the cap is genuinely mutual and that Customer's payment obligation carve-out (21.3) does not operate against us.

No indemnity section appears in the outline: Section 20 is missing entirely although Section 9.3 cross-references "Section 20.5" for IP infringement remedies and 21.3 references "indemnification obligations." Confirm the absence of any Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity before marking missing; the dangling cross-references support a gap.

Section 12.4 (second instance) bars Customer from developing, marketing, selling or acquiring competing products for the term plus 24 months in any territory — a direct breach of the no-restriction position. Note the conflict with Section 12.3, which states Customer has made no non-compete commitment.

Section 12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to engage any supplier and disclaims exclusivity. Section 7.2 (first instance) imposes a disclose-and-match obligation before engaging another provider, which functions as a de facto exclusivity/right-of-first-refusal constraint; assess there rather than duplicating under MFN if the same term is redlined once.

Section 7.2 (first instance) requires Customer to disclose and match any more favourable offer received — an MFN running against us, the wrong direction. Section 12.3 disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment and conflicts with it.

Section 12.4 (first instance) is a one-way 24-month bar on soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee "regardless of how the employee applies" — no general-advertising carve-out and not mutual. Section 12.3 preserves hiring from general recruitment and conflicts.

Section 9 contains only cause-based, insolvency and Customer-specific triggers (9.3) plus force-majeure exit (27.3); no termination for convenience on notice appears, and Section 2.1 expressly denies reduction or termination rights. Check for a Section 9.4 that is not in the outline before concluding it is missing.

Section 8.2 gives a 30-day non-renewal window with a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension if the reminder is missed; Section 8.3 caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant — verify the notice window against the playbook parameter.

Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list — while Section 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts. Flag the direct conflict and the non-accepted governing law; 28.3 escalation is unobjectionable.

Section 24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and change of control; 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on our change of control. Favourable to us — confirm nothing in 24.3 undercuts 24.1.

Section 14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP, but Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence — contrary to owning what we pay for. Read against 13.2 and 14.3 (perpetual licence to embedded Vendor Technology) when assessing.

Sections 13.1–13.3 cover Affiliates and contractors, grant a perpetual paid-up licence to delivered Vendor Technology, permit transfer to Affiliates/successors and limit revocation to material uncured breach after cure. Note that the revocable Deliverable licence in 14.2 conflicts, but address revocability once — likely under IP.

Section 22 limits Vendor audits to once per 12 months with 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, Vendor cost unless a >5% underpayment, and no direct system or unrelated-data access. Likely compliant.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer appears; 7.3 bars interest on amounts not due and 27.3 allows termination without penalty. The nearest economic exposure is the take-or-pay in 2.1, which belongs under MINCOMMIT rather than being flagged twice here.

Section 19 provides professional-services, conformance (90 days for Deliverables, full term for hosted Services), no-malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties, with repair/re-perform then terminate-and-refund in 19.4 and a non-exclusive remedy statement. Likely compliant; check 19.5's disclaimer does not undercut the express warranties.

Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' compensation, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5M cyber cover for the term plus one year; 18.2 adds certificates, primary status and a no-limitation-of-liability statement. Present and likely compliant — compare limits to playbook thresholds.

Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay for three years expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely against the no-take-or-pay-without-exit position, and inconsistent with Section 12.3's disclaimer of minimum-volume commitments.

Section 10.1 references an "agreed transition period" and 10.2 covers Deliverable delivery and refunds, but neither obligates Vendor to return or export Customer Data or provide transition assistance; 16.5 addresses only Confidential Information return and points to Sections 11 and 15 (Section 11 is absent from the outline). Assess whether a usable data-return/exit-assistance obligation exists at all.
